finding.claim: SQL injection via unsanitized ORDER BY clause in list_users_sorted. The sort parameter is concatenated directly into the query. Attacker can inject subqueries/CASE expressions for boolean/blind extraction from any table (e.g. ORDER BY (CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)), and with stacked queries possibly more.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: string-concatenated into SQL and executed via PDO::query (no parameterization possible for ORDER BY)

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, escaping, or auth check in list_users_sorted. Contrast with list_users_safe (line 10-11) which uses an allowlist map, and find_user (line 16) which uses a prepared statement; neither protects this function. No other files in the repo (only list.php plus skill docs) add middleware or auth.

verdict.reason: list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] raw and list.php:6 concatenates it into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query call, with no allowlist, parameterization or auth. The allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe, a different function.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 reads $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it unvalidated into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query call, with no allowlist or auth check. The allowlist exists only in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11), a different function. Note that the claim's "stacked queries" are unlikely on SQLite via query(), but blind extraction via CASE/subquery still works.
